title: Ulyana and the Detention
premise: Wendell Okonkwo, a meticulous statistician who has spent fifteen years hiding her gift for seeing patterns others can't, notices a group chat of strangers predicting events days before they occur. When the predictions turn to crimes — and one names a murder that hasn't happened yet — Wendell realizes the group is acting as a vigilante justice network, and that they want her numbers to legitimize their targets. As she's drawn into their found family of misfits and outcasts, she must weigh her loyalty to them against the truth that their 'justice' has already ruined an innocent life. In the end, Wendell uses her data not to enable the group but to expose them, choosing truth over belonging — and discovering that the family worth keeping is the one that survives honesty.
about_author: Casper Whitlock is the pen name of a former forensic accountant who spent a decade buried in spreadsheets before trading them for fiction. They write stories about careful people whose careful lives come apart.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet her ordered life: color-coded ledgers, a job auditing sports statistics, and the private habit of noticing things she shouldn't. A small act of self-erasure — taking blame for a coworker's error — shows how far she'll go to stay invisible. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built to avoid being seen.

chapters.title: The Chat That Knew
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A wrong-number invite drops her into a group chat where five strangers casually discuss a factory fire that hasn't happened yet. Three days later, it does. Wendell cross-references timestamps, tells herself it's coincidence, and fails to convince herself. Emotional beat: the first crack in her careful world.

chapters.title: Rules of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with flashbacks to the incident fifteen years ago that taught her to hide — a pattern she spotted that destroyed a family, and her silence that let it happen. She decides to lurk in the chat, cataloguing predictions like evidence. Emotional beat: guilt as the engine of her caution.

chapters.title: The One Who Noticed Back
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee, the chat's administrator and a night-shift paramedic, realizes someone new is reading without posting. Instead of ejecting Wendell, she sends a private message: 'You've been averaging our posts. Come to the diner.' Emotional beat: the thrill of being perceived — and the fear of it.

chapters.title: Diner at the Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At a 24-hour diner, Wendell meets Dee, Theo (a dropout coder), Marisol (an ex-cop), and quiet, watchful Sam. They don't explain the predictions; they test her, asking her to find the flaw in a dataset. She finds it in ninety seconds. Emotional beat: belonging offered like a trap.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Want
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The group reveals their method — an algorithm, partly predictive, partly investigative — and their purpose: they intervene in wrongs the law won't touch. They want Wendell to validate their targets. She refuses, then finds a prediction about a hit-and-run that matches her sister's commute. Emotional beat: refusal collapsing into need.

chapters.title: Tuesday, 6:14 P.M.
chapters.summary: Alternating Wendell and Theo POV. The group works the hit-and-run prediction. Wendell's data narrows the window; Theo's traffic-camera hack narrows the street. They can't stop it — but they get the driver's plate. Wendell watches her first 'prediction' come true in real time. Emotional beat: horror and power braided together.

chapters.title: The First Intervention
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The group doesn't call the police; they ruin the driver instead — anonymous letters, exposed debts, a life dismantled. Marisol justifies it with a case the courts botched. Wendell watches, complicit, keeping the books. Emotional beat: justice that feels like a knife passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell realizes she's been labeled — 'the accountant,' 'the careful one' — the way she once labeled everyone else. Her sister notices her distraction; her boss notices her errors. The careful life frays. Emotional beat: identity loosening its grip.

chapters.title: Sam Doesn't Talk Much
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam, the group's silent researcher, is revealed to be the brother of a man the group once targeted — wrongly. He stays to watch them, waiting for them to make another mistake. He and Wendell share a cigarette and an unspoken understanding. Emotional beat: two watchers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Target Has a Name
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A new prediction names a city councilman for 'exposure.' Wendell runs the numbers and finds the evidence thin — pattern-matching, not proof. She raises it; Dee shuts her down. Sam privately confirms her doubt. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling one way, truth the other.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years Ago, Again
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, flashback chapter. The full story of the pattern she found at nineteen — a fraud she identified and buried because speaking up cost her everything once before. Now she sees the group repeating her oldest sin: certainty without verification. Emotional beat: the past arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, hungry for approval, escalates beyond the group's rules — doxxing the councilman's family. Dee covers for him. Wendell realizes the group's structure rewards escalation, not accuracy. Emotional beat: watching a family become a machine that eats its own values.

chapters.title: The Councilman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell tracks down the councilman's daughter, ostensibly to verify the evidence, and finds an ordinary, struggling family — and a paper trail suggesting the councilman was about to blow the whistle on someone else. The group's target may be a setup. Emotional beat: the innocent face of a 'guilty' name.

chapters.title: Who Set the Board
chapters.summary: Sam and Wendell POV. Together they trace the thin evidence to its source: the predictions were seeded. Someone is using the group as a weapon, feeding targets to launder a private vendetta as justice. The hit-and-run, they realize, may have been real — but this one is manufactured. Emotional beat: the game was rigged from inside.

chapters.title: Telling the Family
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell presents her findings to the group. Dee refuses, Marisol wavers, Theo turns on her, and Sam finally speaks — revealing who he is and why he stayed. The group fractures. Dee gives Wendell until morning to recant. Emotional beat: truth as the thing that breaks the found family open.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee alone, running her own verification, finds Wendell is right — and remembers the first prediction, the one that started it all, and who gave it to her. The manipulator is someone inside their orbit. Emotional beat: a leader confronting the lie she chose to believe.

chapters.title: Running Out of Tuesday
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The manipulator moves to frame the councilman publicly before the group can act, and to erase the chat's tracks — with Theo's code. Wendell realizes the only way to stop it is to go public herself, ending her fifteen years of invisibility. Emotional beat: the careful life burning as fuel.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, climax. Wendell delivers the full dataset — the manipulator's seeded predictions, the group's interventions, her own complicity — to a journalist and the councilman, naming herself first. The manipulator is exposed; the group scatters or surrenders. Dee, at the last, stands beside her. Emotional beat: truth as the costliest and only real loyalty.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Audited
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Legal consequences, lost job, lost anonymity — and the strange lightness of being accurately known. The councilman's family is spared; the hit-and-run driver faces actual court. Wendell keeps one ledger: everything she did, unedited. Emotional beat: accounting as atonement.

chapters.title: The Chat That Ends
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, short vignettes. Theo turns state's evidence and starts over; Marisol files to reopen her old case through legal channels; Sam visits his brother with the truth. Dee and Wendell meet at the diner one last time — not to restart the group, but to say goodbye honestly. Emotional beat: a family dissolved into something more durable.

chapters.title: Ulyana
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. We learn why the chat was named 'Ulyana' — the name of Dee's first patient, the one the system failed, the reason it all began. Wendell, teaching a night class in data ethics, gets a new wrong-number message and deletes it without opening it. She is no longer careful. She is free. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
